facts.statement: The fossil of this dinosaur was discovered by Yevgeny Kurochkin in 1982.
facts.quote: It was discovered by Yevgeny Kurochkin in 1982.

facts.statement: All published cladistic analyses place this species within Ornithuromorpha, a group that includes modern birds but excludes Enantiornithes.
facts.quote: Ambiortus dementjevi belongs to Ornithuromorpha, the natural group containing modern birds but not Enantiornithes, according to all published cladistic analyses.

facts.statement: Scientists have debated the exact position of this species within the Ornithuromorpha group.
facts.quote: The exact position of the species within this group has been controversial.

facts.statement: Some studies suggest this species is closely related to Ichthyornithes, a group of birds closely related to modern birds.
facts.quote: Some studies have found it to be closely related to the Ichthyornithes, a relatively derived group closely related to modern birds.

facts.statement: Most analyses classify this species as either an unresolved member of Ornithurae or a more basal member of Ornithuromorpha.
facts.quote: Most analyses have found it to be either an unresolved member of the Ornithurae, or a more basal member of Ornithuromorpha.

facts.statement: The family Ambiortidae is sometimes assigned to this genus, particularly when it is considered a close relative of the younger Apsaravis.
facts.quote: The family Ambiortidae is sometimes used for this genus, especially if it is considered a close relative of the much younger Apsaravis.

facts.statement: A 2011 cladistic analysis indicates that Apsaravis and Palintropus are very closely related to this species.
facts.quote: Los resultados de un análisis cladístico publicado en 2011, por otro lado, indican que al menos Apsaravis y Palintropus (el cual fue considerado erróneamente como un ave mucho más moderna) están muy cercanamente relacionados con este.

facts.statement: The time range for this genus is estimated from 132.6 to 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Barremian (132.6 to 121.4 million years ago)
